1.title: Cut off one clear plug
1.say: Lay the thick blue cable flat on the table. Cut one clear plug off right at the plug.
placements: clear plug on one end of the thick blue cable → cut off with cutters applied flush at the plug base and discarded, leaving a flat cut bare end on the cable (in the video: blue coiled cable on dark table with one clear plug kept and the other end flat cut)
watch_for: if both ends have no plug you cut off both plugs, so you must start with a cable that still has one plug
if a long stub of plug plastic remains the cut was too far out, recut flush to leave a clean flat end
1.check_yourself: It should look like a coiled blue cable with one clear plug on one end and a flat cut bare end on the other.
1.safety: Keep your fingers clear of the cutter blades and cut away from your body.

2.title: Peel outer cover back an inch
2.say: Hold the cut end of the thick blue cable steady. Peel the outer blue cover back about one inch.
placements: outer blue cover at the flat cut end of the thick blue cable → slit and pulled off about one inch with the yellow handled stripping tool applied about one inch from the tip, exposing eight little coloured wires (in the video: blue cable on dark wood table with colour wires sticking out)
watch_for: if you see nicks in the little coloured wires you squeezed too hard, strip a fresh bit further down
if less than a finger nail of wire shows the cover is still too long, peel back to about one inch
2.check_yourself: It should look like eight small coloured wires sticking out about one inch from the blue outer cover.
2.safety: Keep your fingers out of the stripper jaws and close the tool slowly.

3.title: Untwist and straighten all wires
3.say: Spread the eight little coloured wires apart with your fingers. Untwist each one and pull it straight.
placements: white filler string among the inner wires → snipped off at the edge of the outer blue cover and discarded (in the video: small white bit on dark wood table)

eight twisted coloured inner wires fanning from the outer blue cover → separated with fingers, untwisted and pulled straight with no twists left (in the video: eight straight wires fanning on dark wood table)
watch_for: if wires still curl in pairs they are still twisted, you will not be able to line them flat
if a wire kinks sharply when you pull it you pulled too hard, smooth it gently straight again
3.check_yourself: It should look like eight straight little wires fanning out with no twists from the blue outer cover.

4.title: Slide small cover onto cable
4.say: Pick up the small blue cover with the wide opening facing the wires. Push it down the thick blue cable past the wires.
placements: small blue ribbed cover with wide opening on one end → slid over the wire tips down the thick blue cable to sit below the exposed wires with wide opening facing up toward the tips (in the video: blue boot around blue cable below colour wires on dark wood table)
watch_for: if the small blue cover is past the wire tips toward the far plug you put it on the wrong end, slide it onto the cut end
if the narrow closed end faces the wire tips it is backwards and will not cover the plug, flip it so the wide opening faces the tips
4.check_yourself: It should look like a small blue cover sitting around the blue cable below the loose coloured wires.

5.title: Line up wires green first
5.say: Line up white with green stripe and green and white with orange stripe and blue. Add white with blue stripe and orange and white with brown stripe and brown. Trim the ends straight across so all eight match.
placements: eight straight inner wires from the outer blue cover → arranged flat side by side left to right in green first order: white with green stripe and green and white with orange stripe and blue and white with blue stripe and orange and white with brown stripe and brown, matching the 568A diagram shown on screen (in the video: green first fan held over a finger with brown on the far right)
wire tips → trimmed straight across even with cutters so all eight ends are equal and short for plug entry (in the video: flat even parallel tips ready to insert)
watch_for: if orange comes before green the order is orange first and will make the wrong end, swap to green first
if the tips are different lengths some wires will miss the front, retrim straight across
5.check_yourself: It should look like eight flat parallel wires in green first order with even tips ready to push in.
5.safety: Keep your fingers behind the cutter blades when you trim the ends.

6.title: Push wires fully into plug
6.say: Hold the clear plug with the open end facing the wires. Push the eight little wires all the way to the front.
placements: eight ordered flat wires with even tips → pushed into the back opening of the new clear plug until each coloured tip reaches the very front wall under the gold teeth, with blue outer cover edge just inside the plug rear (in the video: clear plug on wire ends on dark wood table with colours visible to the front)
watch_for: if colours change order inside the plug the wires crossed while pushing, pull out and line them flat again
if wire tips stop short of the front the connection will fail, push harder until all touch the front
6.check_yourself: It should look like a clear plug on the wire ends with all coloured wires visible reaching the front.

7.title: Squeeze plug tight with tool
7.say: Set the clear plug into the front slot of the orange handled squeezing tool. Squeeze the handles hard to lock it.
placements: clear plug holding wires with blue outer cover tucked inside rear → seated fully in the front slot of the orange handled black squeezing tool and squeezed hard to press gold teeth down and lock the plug (in the video: plug inserted in crimp tool head over dark wood table)
watch_for: if the plug pulls off with a gentle tug it was not squeezed hard enough, reseat and squeeze again
if the blue outer cover hangs outside the plug the cable will break, push cover inside before squeezing
7.check_yourself: It should look like a flattened clear plug locked onto the wires with blue outer cover pinched inside the back.
7.safety: Keep your fingers out of the tool jaws when you squeeze the handles.

8.title: Slide cover up over plug
8.say: Hold the thick blue cable steady. Push the small blue cover up over the back of the clear plug.
placements: small blue ribbed cover sitting below on the thick blue cable → slid up the cable and over the rear of the crimped clear plug until it covers the back of the plug (in the video: blue boot covering back of clear plug on dark wood table, finished crossover end)
watch_for: if the clear plug back is still exposed the cover is still low on the cable, push it fully up
if the cover twists the wires it was forced sideways, slide straight up without turning
8.check_yourself: It should look like the blue cover hugging the back of the clear plug on the finished end.
